title: CF Meet notification event envelope v1 (cfmeet.notifications.event)
description: Envelope every producer posts to the Notification Service (I1, ingestNotificationEvents) from its transactional outbox, built with packages/notification-client (Document 4 §5). Aligned with cfmeet.platform.event-envelope. Rules beyond JSON Schema, enforced by notification-client and I1: total size ≤ 4 KiB (≤ 8 KiB with `sealed`); `producer` equals the authenticated service identity; the service accepts the current and previous eventVersion per type. `data` keys are camelCase and never contain secret, private, token, ciphertext, plaintext, content, body, password, email, phone, key or code (any case): such values travel only inside `sealed`, and `sealed` is allowed only for the catalogue types that declare it (#21–#25, #32–#38), with exactly the catalogue's `sealed` fields plus any of its `sealedOptional` fields. CRITICAL priority is allowed only for account.* types from cfmeet.meeting-service. Email categories that exist today carry today's idempotency key formats. Every event carries the producer's routing-fence decision (`route`). The control event notifications.cancel cancels pending items by cancelKey. A catalogue entry naming a `recipient` kind requires exactly one recipient of that kind. The catalogue is also published machine-readably under x-cfmeet-catalogue.

the alert of a sign-in from a device not seen recently (key new-sign-in:<session id>): one email principal with the address sealed, ACCOUNT subject; the client label and masked network the email shows are sealed (requestClient / requestNetwork), never data

an email change attempted to an address that already has an account (key email-in-use:<recipient hash>:<hour>): one email principal with the address sealed and no subject, so the event never names the account

the email-changed notices (key email-changed:{old,new}:<change id>): side OLD to the previous address with the masked new address sealed and, for a self-service change, the undo token sealed (no token: the support-assisted change); side NEW to the new address; one email principal with the address sealed, ACCOUNT subject
